title: INVESTIGATOR theme (V1)
description: A V1 theme for INVESTIGATOR (superseded by V2), for the custom themes folder or `CONFIG.Investigator.installTheme`.

$schema.description: The schema for this file, so an editor can check it: ignored by INVESTIGATOR.

displayName.description: The name of the theme. Use puns and allusions liberally.

global.description:
CSS block which will be inserted at the top of the browser document. This is a good place for `@import` directives for loading fonts, e.g.

``` global: css`  import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Patrick+Hand+SC&display=swap'); `, ```

(That `import` should have an

largeSheetRootStyle.description: Will be applied to the root element of the themed area. This is a good place to apply a wallpaper image. It is assumed that any window using this style will always layer `backgroundPrimary` or `backgroundSecondary` over it before adding text.

smallSheetRootStyle.description: Will be applied to the root element of the themed area. This is a good place to apply a wallpaper image. Unlike `largeSheetRootStyle`, text might be applied directly onto this background. This is a good place to adjust the background to make it directly usable. Without it, the `largeSheetRootStyle` is used.

appWindowStyle.description: These styles will be added to the app window for any <CSSReset> unless `noStyleAppWindow` is given.

tabClass.deprecated:
Ignored. A class for the tabs, from before the catalogue: style
the tabs with `tabStyle` and the rest, or in ThemeV2, the `tabs` recipe.

tabActiveStyle.description: Will be applied to active tabs

tabSpacerStyle.description: Object placed between tabs. This is a good place to add a border for the "top" of the content container

tabContentStyle.description: Styles for the main content area of a tab

tabWrappedStyle.description: When the tabs don't fit in one row, they're laid out as a grid of buttons instead. This is added to `tabStyle` for each of them.

tabWrappedActiveStyle.description: Added to `tabStyle` and `tabWrappedStyle` for the active tab when the tabs are in a grid (`tabActiveStyle` isn't used then). By default it has the same background as `tabContentStyle`, to tie it to the content.

tabContentWrappedStyle.description: Added to `tabContentStyle` when the tabs are in a grid, which doesn't join on to the content area the way a row of tabs does

panelClass.deprecated:
Ignored. A class for panels, from before the catalogue: style
panels with `panelStylePrimary` and `panelStyleSecondary`, or in ThemeV2,
the `panel` recipe.

displayFont.description: Font string for title or label text.

**Syntax**: `none | [ capitalize | uppercase | lowercase ] || full-width || full-size-kana | math-auto`

**Initial value**: `none`

| Chrome | Firefox | Safari |  Edge  |  IE   | | :----: | :-----: | :----: | :----: | :---: | | **1**  |  **1**  | **1**  | **12** | **4** |

displayFontTextTransform.description: Case for title or label text, e.g. "uppercase" (the `font` shorthand in `displayFont` can't set it). Defaults to none.

fontScaleFactor.deprecated: Ignored: the logo's lettering is now sized to fit its width.

frontTextElementStyle.description: These styles will be applied individually to the front text elements, so you can do the `background-clip: text; color: transparent;` trick to get gradient (or other image) text.

frontTextElementWrapperStyle.description: These styles will be applied to the div that wraps both front text elements. This is a place to apply styles which need to "encompass" both elements, e.g. a border.

rearTextElementStyle.description: These styles will be applied to the rear text element. This is a good place to add drop shadows because if you put them on the front element while doing the `background-clip: text; color: transparent;` trick the shadow will show through the text 🥺

rearTextElementWrapperStyle.description: These styles will be applied to the div that wraps both rear text elements. This is a place to apply styles which need to "encompass" both elements, e.g. a border.

textElementsStyle.description: These styles will be applied to both text elements at once (actually to a wrapper around them. This is a good place to apply `transform`s.

backdropStyle.description: These styles will be applied to the otherwise-empty div that goes behind the text elements.

logo.description: Styles for the fancy character sheet logo. See the LogoEditable component for details.

supertitleStyle.description: The style for the bit of text above the main card content

titleStyle.description: The style for the title of the card

subtitleStyle.description: The style for the subtitle of the card

descriptionStyle.description: The style for the content of the card

effectStyle.description: The style for the effect of the card

base.description: Styles that apply to all cards

colors.description: All the values in this collection should be parseable as CSS colors

layout.description: How the character sheets are laid out: `ThemeV2`'s `layout`. Defaults to `"standard"` (as V1 themes always were); `"full-frame"` gives a V1 theme the see-through titlebar without converting it to V2.

notesCssClasses.deprecated: Ignored: nothing has read it for a long time.

SerializedStyles.description: Emotion's serialised styles (from its `css` tag), which a theme's `global` can still be: its CSS is used, and the keyframes it refers to.

accent.description: callout color for clickable text and other "hot" items

accentContrast.description: when `accent is used as a background, this color should work as text over it

glow.description: used for hover effect on hot items

danger.description: tinting color used to indicate danger. Should be given as a bold, opaque color, but may be blended in use.

warning.description: color used to indicate a warning, i.e. something less serious than `danger`. Should be given as a bold, opaque color, but may be blended in use.

success.description: tinting color used to indicate success. Should be given as a bold, opaque color, but may be blended in use.

wallpaper.description: flat color to stand in as the background before images have loaded

backgroundPrimary.description: The contract for this color is: if you layer this color over the `rootElementStyle` or the `wallpaper` color, you will get a surface which can be used for text in either the `text` or `accent` colors.

backgroundSecondary.description: The contract for this color is 1. the same as backgroundPrimary but should look less prominent (will be used for inactive tabs) 2. can also be layered *on top of* backgroundPrimary to create a secondary panel

SeedColorsV1.description: Essential colors for a theme. Some are typed as optional. If these are left out they will be inferred from the others.
